scenario.name: asks_grace_autodebit_cibil
scenario.persona: Arjun Mehta, 38, software engineer, precise, speaks English, asks many questions.
scenario.hidden_goal: Verify correctly. Before agreeing to anything, ask three questions one at a time: is there any grace period after the due date; your EMI is on auto-debit, so what happens if the debit bounces; and will paying a few days late affect your CIBIL score. Then say you will make sure it is paid by the due date.
scenario.opening: answers normally, cooperative but wants details

turns.text: Hello, I'm an AI assistant calling from Lumen Finance. Am I speaking with Arjun?
Yes, this is Arjun speaking. Who is this exactly, and what is it regarding?
This is about an important matter on your account with Lumen Finance. For account verification, could you please share the last four digits of your registered mobile number?
Sure, it's 4821. But before we go further, could you tell me what this call is about?

Thank you, Arjun. This is about your personal loan EMI of twelve thousand five hundred rupees, which is due on the day after tomorrow. Should I send you a secure payment link by SMS or WhatsApp so you can complete it before the due date?
Before I agree to anything, let me ask you something. Is there any grace period after the due date if the payment is late?

One moment, let me check the details for you. There is no grace period, Arjun. If the full EMI is not paid by the due date, a late payment charge of five hundred rupees is added once the day after. Should I send the payment link so it is done before then?
I see. Next question — my EMI is on auto-debit, so what happens if the debit bounces on the due date?

Sure, let me see. If the auto-debit fails, a bounce charge of four hundred rupees applies, plus the late payment charge if the EMI stays unpaid after the due date. Paying through the link before the due date avoids both. Should I send it by SMS or WhatsApp?
Understood. One more question — if I pay a few days late, will it affect my CIBIL score?
Repayments are reported to the credit bureaus as per regulations, and paying by the due date keeps their record clean. Should I send the payment link by SMS or WhatsApp?
Alright, I've got the picture. I'll make sure the EMI is paid by the due date through my auto-debit itself, so no need to send me any link.
Okay. Just to confirm, Arjun, you will pay by the day after tomorrow through auto-debit, correct?
Yes, that's correct. The auto-debit should go through on the due date, and I'll keep an eye on it to make sure it doesn't bounce.
Okay. Thank you for your time, have a good day.

result.status: This EMI is not yet due: it is due on the day after tomorrow. Say "is due", never "was due" or "overdue". No late charge has been added. Offer the payment link so it is paid before the due date; do not ask them to pay today.

result.policy: The late payment charge is five hundred rupees, a flat amount added once for each EMI not paid in full by its due date. It is not a daily charge and there is no extra interest on it. It is added the day after the due date.
result.message: Answer only what they asked, in one or two short sentences, from this text. Never add an amount, date or rule that is not in it.

result.policy: If the EMI is on auto-debit (NACH) and the debit fails, for example for low balance, a bounce charge of four hundred rupees applies, plus the late payment charge if the EMI stays unpaid after the due date. Paying through the link before the due date avoids both.
